profile_name: Mariana Souza — Senior Backend / ML Engineer

facts.content: At Acme Logistics, led migration of a Django monolith to FastAPI microservices on AWS ECS, reducing p99 latency from 850ms to 410ms over six months.
At Acme Logistics, built event-driven ETL pipelines in Python using Apache Airflow and Kafka, processing 30TB/day of vehicle telemetry data.
At Acme Logistics, mentored 4 junior engineers, two of whom were promoted to mid-level within 12 months.
At Northwind Retail, designed and shipped a product-recommendation service using sentence-transformers embeddings and pgvector, lifting checkout CTR by 9.4% in A/B test.
At Northwind Retail, owned the catalog search rewrite from Postgres FTS to a hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval stack served by FastAPI.
At Northwind Retail, reduced AWS spend by 22% by right-sizing RDS, switching idle EC2 to spot, and adding CloudWatch dashboards for the data team.
At StartLab (acquired 2020), built the company's first ML platform on GCP — Vertex AI Pipelines for training, Cloud Run for inference, BigQuery for the feature store.
Open-sourced 'fastrag', a small library for evaluating RAG pipelines (P@k, R@k, MRR, hallucination rate via LLM judge). 480 GitHub stars.
Built a tool-calling agent in 200 lines that translates natural-language analytics questions to SQL against a Postgres warehouse; demoed at PyCon Brazil 2023.
Contributed a pgvector benchmark suite to the official repo, comparing IVFFlat vs HNSW recall across 1M-vector workloads.
BSc Computer Science, Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, graduated 2017.
Cloud platforms: AWS (ECS, RDS, S3, Lambda) and GCP (Cloud Run, Vertex AI, BigQuery).
Retrieval and embeddings: pgvector, sentence-transformers, BM25, hybrid retrieval with RRF.
LLMs and agents: OpenAI API, Anthropic API, function/tool calling, multi-step reasoning, prompt engineering.
Knowledge graphs: experimented with Neo4j and a custom Postgres adjacency-list graph for skill expansion.
Speaker at PyCon Brazil 2023 on 'Evaluating RAG without lying to yourself'.
